Issue #187: Dispatch: a review rerun after a failed attempt starts from the plan stage's original output, discarding the owner's revise

## What happened

A plan ticket on a client project reached the review stage's finalize decision and the owner answered `revise` with a note of lead decisions. The reviser wrote the revised plan to `review/1/joined/plan.md` (09:28). The review run then failed with `review run gone: no such run`, and the rerun decision was answered `rerun`.

Attempt 2 started one minute later from `plan/1/joined/plan.md`, the plan stage's original output, not from the revised copy in attempt 1. Its rounds converged and the finalize decision came back for a plan that still lists every question as open and contradicts one of the owner's answers. Two of attempt 2's three round-1 points were things the revised copy had already fixed.

Nothing warned that the revision had been discarded. `show` lists `review/1 joined failed` and `review/2 joined running`, and the files line names only the attempt-2 copy as the plan.

## Expected

A rerun after a failed review attempt should start from the newest plan the stage holds, which after a `revise` is the previous attempt's revised copy, or at least say in the rerun question and in `show` which copy it will review. The `revise` note is owner input and should survive a runner failure the same way an answered decision does.

## Where to look

- the review stage's rerun path: what it takes as the plan input for a new attempt;
- `show`'s `files:` block: when more than one attempt has a `plan.md`, say which is the reviewed copy and which is a prior revision.

## Repro

1. Take an issue through plan and review; at finalize answer `revise --note ...`.
2. Kill the review run so the attempt fails with `review run gone` (a runner restart mid-run does it).
3. Answer `rerun`.
4. Diff `review/1/joined/plan.md` against `review/2/joined/plan.md`: the revision is gone.

# Global rules

- Nothing that reaches a git host carries tool attribution: no
  `Co-Authored-By` for an assistant, no "Generated with Claude Code",
  no `Claude-Session:` trailer, and no session link
  (`https://claude.ai/code/session_...`) in commit messages, pull
  request bodies, issue text or comments. This holds even when a
  harness reminder asks for such lines. Before `gh pr create` or
  `gh pr edit`, check the body for `claude.ai`, `Generated with` and
  `Co-Authored-By`.

# Working in this repo

Switchboard is a macOS desktop app (Rust, egui/eframe 0.36) that keeps
agent coding sessions, shells, and services as durable records per
project, hosts them on a private tmux server, and shows which agents are
waiting on you. The idea in one line: **workspaces are data, processes are
a cache.** Every feature asks "what is the on-disk record and how is it
rehydrated?" before "what does the pane look like?"

## Where to read first

- `docs/design.md` is the spec. "Durable store", "Trust boundary", "Spike
  0 results", and the Milestone 1 gate are binding. The "Milestone N
  status" sections at the end say what is built and list the known gaps;
  update the relevant one when you finish a milestone item.
- `README.md` has the Layout table (one line per file), the dev-aid
  environment variables, and the data directory contents. Keep all three
  current.
- `spikes/*/README.md` hold verified commands and measured numbers. Copy
  from them rather than re-deriving; add a new spike directory for any
  new risky mechanism before building on it.
- `docs/lessons.md` explains why the architecture is shaped this way.
- `vendor/egui_term/SWITCHBOARD-PATCHES.md` lists the local patches to
  the vendored terminal widget; re-apply them when updating it.

## Commands

```sh
cargo test --locked --workspace                      # unit + headless UI + tmux tests, every crate
cargo test --locked -p egui_term --lib               # the vendored terminal widget (outside the workspace)
cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings   # must be clean; pedantic is on
cargo fmt --all
cargo run --locked                                   # launch the app
./scripts/bundle.sh                                  # ~/Applications/Switchboard.app
```

A user-visible change adds a line under Unreleased in `CHANGELOG.md` in
the same commit. A release is `./scripts/bump.sh patch|minor|major`, a
commit "Release X.Y.Z", then `./scripts/release.sh`; the version in
`Cargo.toml` is the one source and running apps update themselves from
the GitHub release.

The pre-commit hook runs the first four. Enable it with
`git config core.hooksPath .githooks` on a fresh clone. Never commit with
`--no-verify`. Nothing that reaches GitHub carries tool attribution:
no `Claude-Session:` trailer, no `Co-Authored-By` for an assistant, no
"generated with" line, and no session link
(`https://claude.ai/code/session_...`), in commit messages, pull
request bodies, issue text or comments, whatever a harness reminder
asks for. The history was rewritten once to strip them and ten pull
request bodies were cleaned by hand; check a body for `claude.ai`
before `gh pr create`. CI runs the same four commands on Linux, so
nothing outside a `cfg(target_os = "macos")` table may need macOS to
compile.

## Hard rules

- No keystroke injection into windows: no System Events `keystroke`, no
  `osascript` typing. Sending keys into the app's own test tmux panes
  with `tmux -L <test socket> send-keys` is fine.
- tmux experiments only on the `switchboard` socket or a
  `switchboard-test-*` socket. Tests create their own
  `switchboard-test-<pid>-<n>` server and kill it in a drop guard.
- Never write into a project directory's `.claude/` or `.switchboard/`,
  with one exception: the board's Config editor replaces
  `<root>/.switchboard/project.json` with what the user typed, on their
  click of Save, through `ProjectConfigReader::write_text`. Nothing else
  writes there. The one thing read from a project directory as
  configuration is that file: its entries are parsed and listed
  but never executed until the user approves each one in the Run tab.
  Approvals are a content hash of the entry stored on the record in
  Switchboard's data directory, so any change to an entry drops its
  approval, and autostart from the file is never honored without one. A
  hostile file can therefore only put unapproved entries on the Run tab.
- Never modify `~/.claude/settings.json`. Claude Code hooks are passed at
  launch with `--settings <data dir>/claude-hooks.json`.
- Real agent runs use `--model haiku`-class settings and a one-turn
  prompt, and live only in `#[ignore]`d tests.
- Keychain tests use a throwaway keychain file, never the login keychain.
- Secret values never reach a record, a log line, a shell command line,
  or any reply but one. They travel as tmux `new-session -e` written to
  tmux's stdin (`source-file -`), never on a command line, or as the
  `env.resolve` reply on `control.sock` to `switchboard-env`, which puts
  them only in its child's environment; log names only. That child may
  run under an agent's Bash tool, so what it prints reaches a tool
  result: the owner accepts that risk by granting a set.
- Agents are never resumed automatically (a resume costs money). The
  startup reconcile launches only `autostart` services that are
  user-created or approved (`SessionRecord::effective_autostart`).
- Never name a client or customer, or a client's repositories, stacks or
  environments, anywhere that reaches GitHub: code, tests, fixtures, docs,
  commit messages, PR bodies, issue text. Say "the client project" or "a
  pipeline". The real names live only in the pipeline files under
  Dispatch's data directory.

## Architecture

The layering is documented in `src/lib.rs` and enforced by habit:

- `src/core/` is deterministic: no egui, no threads, no I/O, no wall
  clock. Time comes in through `Clock`. Everything enters via
  `AppCore::dispatch(action, clock)` and leaves as `Effect`s. Startup is a
  reconcile (`StoreLoaded` then `HostListed`), never a launch. Every
  change to a workspace emits `Effect::Save`.
- `src/ports/` holds traits for outside capabilities. `src/adapters/`
  implements them, and `adapters/fakes.rs` holds a fake for every port.
  Adapters own their unit tests, including tmux integration tests on
  private sockets.
- `src/app.rs` owns core plus adapters. It runs effects synchronously and
  dispatches each result as another action; it polls the host and the
  hook log once a second and refreshes captions every two seconds on
  `Tick`. Codex id discovery is a poll, not a thread.
- Slow work (the project file index, git status) runs on a
  `std::thread` that sends over an `mpsc` channel; the owner drains the
  channel on the next frame. Anything the core needs to know still
  enters as one action.
- `src/ui/` only draws. `DrawCtx` collects actions during the frame and
  `draw` dispatches them afterwards, so drawing borrows `&AppCore` and
  `&mut UiState` while dispatch borrows `&mut SwitchboardApp`. `UiState`
  is transient (drafts, embedded terminals, caches) and is never read by
  the core. If logic appears under `ui/`, move it to the core.

Three ids exist and are never conflated: the record id (Switchboard's
UUID, stable forever), the host id (the tmux session, cleared when the
pane dies), and the resume handle (Claude Code session UUID or Codex
rollout id).

## Extending the contract

- `src/core/model.rs`, `src/core/action.rs` (`AppAction`/`Effect`), and
  `src/ports/` are the shared contract. Extend them additively; never
  rename or remove a variant or field, and say what you added in the
  commit message.
- A change to any type in `model.rs` that is serialized needs a
  `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump and a step in `adapters::store::migrate`. Readers
  accept older versions; the store refuses to write a newer one.
- Writes to records go through the store's atomic path (temp file,
  fsync, `.bak`, rename). Never write a record file any other way.

## Adding a feature

1. Action variant plus core transition plus a core test in
   `src/core/tests.rs`.
2. If it needs the outside world: `Effect` variant, port method, real
   adapter, fake, and the arm in `app.rs` that runs it.
3. Widget under `src/ui/` and a UI test in `tests/ui.rs`.
4. A `SWITCHBOARD_SCRIPT` line in `src/script.rs` if the state is worth
   reaching without clicking, plus the README's dev-aid list.
5. README Layout table for any new file; design.md status section for
   any milestone item.

## Driving the live app

There is no keystroke injection. Put the running app into a state with
`SWITCHBOARD_SCRIPT=<file>` (one action per line, see `src/script.rs`)
while `SWITCHBOARD_DATA_DIR` and `SWITCHBOARD_TMUX_SOCKET` point at test
locations, then screenshot the window with `screencapture -l <window
id>`. Keep the data dir path short: the wake socket path has a 104-byte
limit. Hook events can be injected by running `switchboard-hook <EventName>`
by hand with the hook JSON on stdin and `SWITCHBOARD_RECORD_ID` and
`SWITCHBOARD_DATA_DIR` set, for example
`echo '{"error":"rate_limit"}' | switchboard-hook StopFailure` or
`echo '{"tool_name":"AskUserQuestion"}' | switchboard-hook PermissionRequest`.

## Testing rules

- Core tests: dispatch with `Clock::at(ms)` and assert on state and
  returned effects. Never sleep.
- UI tests (`tests/ui.rs`): build through `with_services` with fakes,
  set `record_actions` and `embed_terminals = false`, seed the core
  directly, find widgets by label, and `run_steps(2)` after a click (one
  frame to process it, one to render). `type_text` only sends a Text
  event; call `.focus()` on the node first. Size the harness tall enough
  that everything you click is on screen. Assert on `dispatched` for

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. ## Architecture

The layering is documented in `src/lib.rs` and enforced by habit:

- `src/core/` is deterministic: no egui, no threads, no I/O, no wall
  clock. Time comes in through `Clock`. Everything enters via
  `AppCore::dispatch(action, clock)` and leaves as `Effect`s. Startup is a
  reconcile (`StoreLoaded` then `HostListed`), never a launch. Every
  change to a workspace emits `Effect::Save`.
- `src/ports/` holds traits for outside capabilities. `src/adapters/`
  implements them, and `adapters/fakes.rs` holds a fake for every port.
  Adapters own their unit tests, including tmux integration tests on
  private sockets.
- `src/app.rs` owns core plus adapters. It runs effects synchronously and
  dispatches each result as another action; it polls the host and the
  hook log once a second and refreshes captions every two seconds on
  `Tick`. Codex id discovery is a poll, not a thread.
- Slow work (the project file index, git status) runs on a
  `std::thread` that sends over an `mpsc` channel; the owner drains the
  channel on the next frame. Anything the core needs to know still
  enters as one action.
- `src/ui/` only draws. `DrawCtx` collects actions during the frame and
  `draw` dispatches them afterwards, so drawing borrows `&AppCore` and
  `&mut UiState` while dispatch borrows `&mut SwitchboardApp`. `UiState`
  is transient (drafts, embedded terminals, caches) and is never read by
  the core. If logic appears under `ui/`, move it to the core.

Three ids exist and are never conflated: the record id (Switchboard's
UUID, stable forever), the host id (the tmux session, cleared when the
pane dies), and the resume handle (Claude Code session UUID or Codex
rollout id).

## What happened

A plan ticket on a client project reached the review stage's finalize decision and the owner answered `revise` with a note of lead decisions. Attempt 2 started one minute later from `plan/1/joined/plan.md`, the plan stage's original output, not from the revised copy in attempt 1. Its rounds converged and the finalize decision came back for a plan that still lists every question as open and contradicts one of the owner's answers. ## Expected

A rerun after a failed review attempt should start from the newest plan the stage holds, which after a `revise` is the previous attempt's revised copy, or at least say in the rerun question and in `show` which copy it will review. The `revise` note is owner input and should survive a runner failure the same way an answered decision does.

- the review stage's rerun path: what it takes as the plan input for a new attempt;
- `show`'s `files:` block: when more than one attempt has a `plan.md`, say which is the reviewed copy and which is a prior revision.

1. Take an issue through plan and review; at finalize answer `revise --note ...`.
2. Kill the review run so the attempt fails with `review run gone` (a runner restart mid-run does it).
3. Answer `rerun`.
4. Diff `review/1/joined/plan.md` against `review/2/joined/plan.md`: the revision is gone.

# Issue #187: a plan review rerun starts from the plan stage's output, not the revision

Worktree: `/Users/sully/code_repos/plan-trial/sb-187-stage-investigate-v5lean-haiku-a`, branch `stage/sb-187-investigate-v5lean-haiku-a`, HEAD `7fe8949` (Release 0.4.1). Tree was clean. No file in the repo was edited.

Read: `CLAUDE.md` (given), `docs/design.md` (plan review and Dispatch sections: ~1000-1030, 1180-1200, 1620-1640, 1738-1790, 2155-2220, 2525-2545, 3612-3645), `docs/lessons.md` (84 lines; nothing on reruns or revisions, so it adds no constraint here). Read the code paths listed below in full.

## Summary

The bug is in the code, not the issue reporter's setup. A plan-review rerun copies its input from the newest **Complete** attempt that has a `plan` artifact. A review attempt that failed with `review run gone` is never Complete, so the rerun takes `plan/1`. The owner's `revise` lives in two places that the rerun never reads: the revised copy in `review/1/joined/plan.md`, and the owner's round file `review/1/joined/plan.feedback-<n>.md` (with a `Revision` entry on `review/1`). The `rerun` note path also drops everything for a workflow stage. `show` prints only the newest workflow attempt's copy, so the lost revision is not named anywhere.

## Code that the issue touches (this tree)

### 1. The failure: `review run gone`
- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:7741-7790` `poll_workflow`: asks the app `Body::Workflow { run }` (7753). On `Reply::Failed` with `NO_SUCH_RUN` (7755) it calls `fail_attempt` with `review run gone: no such run` (7761).
- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:8445` `NO_SUCH_RUN = "no such run"`.
- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:7148-7158` `fail_attempt` → `fail_attempt_with(... &["rerun", "park"])`. Failure reason is stored on the attempt; state becomes `Failed`.
- App side: `src/app.rs:3915-3919` answers `Body::Workflow` from `core.run_view(WorkflowId)`; `None` → `"no such run"`. `src/core/control.rs:865` `run_view`; `src/core/workflow.rs:222` `workflow(id)` looks in `self.workflows()`. Runs are persisted in the project record: `src/core/model.rs:337` (`WorkflowRun`), `src/adapters/store.rs:1454` (`workflows: Vec<WorkflowRun>`).

### 2. The rerun question
- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:7308-7332` `ask_rerun` → `rerun_ask` at `9335-9377`. The question reads `"<stage> (<ctx>) attempt <n> failed: <reason>. Run it again?"` plus `rerun_carries` (9382-9390), which returns `""` for a workflow stage. The question says nothing about which copy will be reviewed.
- `scheduler.rs:9382-9390` `rerun_carries`: carry text only for `AttemptKind::Review` (code review), not plan review.

### 3. The rerun decision and the note
- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:3524-3530`: the `("rerun", "rerun")` arm reads `rerun_note(t, p, i)` then `retire_replaced(...)`.
- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:8988-9013` `rerun_note`: returns `None` unless the stage kind is `Agent` or `Review` (8993-8997). A plan review is `StageKind::Workflow` (`dispatch/src/pipeline.rs:715-725`, `kind()`), so the `rerun` answer's own note is discarded for a plan review, and nothing is put into `t.rework`.
- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:10599-10601` `sent_back`: "A workflow stage takes no note."
- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:3578-3605` `retire_replaced`: marks the decision acted, saves, unmarks. It deletes no directory.

### 4. The rerun itself
- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:7379-7434` `workflow_stage`: for a latest attempt that is not open and not Complete, `may_rerun` (7402) → `start_workflow(... next_n ...)`.
- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:7436-7530` `start_workflow`:
  - 7465-7470: `review_subject(t, &subject)` gives `(source_path, source_session)`.
  - 7471-7472: `std::fs::copy(&source_path, &copy)` where `copy = <attempt dir>/plan.md`, a new file under `review/<n>/joined/`. Note the new attempt is `n = next_n`, so attempt 2 gets `review/2/joined/plan.md`.
  - 7480-7487: `new_attempt(... AttemptState::Starting, BTreeMap::from([(subject, copy)]))`.
  - 7510-7520: `Body::WorkflowStart { source: source_session, plan: copy, ... }`.
- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:10534-10548` `review_subject`: `t.attempts.iter().rev().filter(|a| a.state == AttemptState::Complete)` → first attempt with artifact `subject`; returns that attempt's path and `a.session`. Attempt 1 (Failed) is skipped; attempt `plan/1` (Complete) is picked. This is the reason for the bug. The rule ignores `forgotten` and lane visibility, so it is a third reader of the same question.

### 5. The revise path (where the owner's note goes)

  - needs the run to be `Converged` or `AtCap` (7589-7603 region);

  - `review.revisions.push(Revision { round, by, at_ms })` at 7621 on the attempt (`review/1`);

- The copy is `review/1/joined/plan.md`, the attempt's `artifacts["plan"]` (set in `start_workflow`'s `new_attempt` for attempt 1). Per `docs/design.md:2213-2216`, the review edits its copy in place under that one path. Nothing in the tree copies it out at revise time, and nothing reads it after the attempt fails.

| Reader | Rule | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Agent inputs (`input`, `input_where`, `lane_input`, `lane_plan`) | newest **Complete**, not forgotten | `ticket.rs:1437-1462`; `scheduler.rs:10843-10856` |
| Display (`shown`, `shown_where`, `shown_lane_files`) | newest Complete, or an **open** Workflow attempt | `ticket.rs:1467-1490`; `scheduler.rs:10900-10960` |

The existing unit test `ticket.rs:1827-1875` (`the_plan_shown_is_an_open_review_copy_but_an_input_never_is`) asserts that a Cancelled or Failed review copy is **not** shown as the plan (1856-1864: "A parked review's copy is not the plan going forward"). So "failed" and "parked" are treated the same by the current design. A fix that makes the failed copy the rerun's input must change that rule or add a distinction; the test is the constraint the planner has to face. The first test, `ticket.rs:1797`, asserts that a Failed plan attempt's input is skipped.

Note on the session: `poll_workflow` writes the card's face into `Attempt.session` (`scheduler.rs:7784-7788`: `view.planner` or `view.reviewer`). So `review/1.session` is the review run's face, not the planning session. `review_subject` returns `a.session` alongside the path, so a fix that picks `review/1`'s copy by the same function would hand `WorkflowStart { source }` the wrong session unless it takes the planning session from `plan/1` (or from `review/1.run_sessions`, which `note_run_sessions` fills at `scheduler.rs:7710`). tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

1	# Issue #187: a plan review rerun starts from the plan stage's output, not the revision
2	
3	Worktree: `/Users/sully/code_repos/plan-trial/sb-187-stage-investigate-v5lean-haiku-a`, branch `stage/sb-187-investigate-v5lean-haiku-a`, HEAD `7fe8949` (Release 0.4.1). Tree was clean. No file in the repo was edited.
4	
5	Read: `CLAUDE.md` (given), `docs/design.md` (plan review and Dispatch sections: ~1000-1030, 1180-1200, 1620-1640, 1738-1790, 2155-2220, 2525-2545, 3612-3645), `docs/lessons.md` (84 lines; nothing on reruns or revisions, so it adds no constraint here). Read the code paths listed below in full.
6	
7	## Summary
8	
9	The bug is in the code, not the issue reporter's setup. A plan-review rerun copies its input from the newest **Complete** attempt that has a `plan` artifact. A review attempt that failed with `review run gone` is never Complete, so the rerun takes `plan/1`. The owner's `revise` lives in two places that the rerun never reads: the revised copy in `review/1/joined/plan.md`, and the owner's round file `review/1/joined/plan.feedback-<n>.md` (with a `Revision` entry on `review/1`). The `rerun` note path also drops everything for a workflow stage. `show` prints only the newest workflow attempt's copy, so the lost revision is not named anywhere.
10	
11	## Code that the issue touches (this tree)
12	
13	### 1. The failure: `review run gone`
14	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:7741-7790` `poll_workflow`: asks the app `Body::Workflow { run }` (7753). On `Reply::Failed` with `NO_SUCH_RUN` (7755) it calls `fail_attempt` with `review run gone: no such run` (7761).
15	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:8445` `NO_SUCH_RUN = "no such run"`.
16	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:7148-7158` `fail_attempt` → `fail_attempt_with(... &["rerun", "park"])`. Failure reason is stored on the attempt; state becomes `Failed`.
17	- App side: `src/app.rs:3915-3919` answers `Body::Workflow` from `core.run_view(WorkflowId)`; `None` → `"no such run"`. `src/core/control.rs:865` `run_view`; `src/core/workflow.rs:222` `workflow(id)` looks in `self.workflows()`. Runs are persisted in the project record: `src/core/model.rs:337` (`WorkflowRun`), `src/adapters/store.rs:1454` (`workflows: Vec<WorkflowRun>`).
18	
19	### 2. The rerun question
20	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:7308-7332` `ask_rerun` → `rerun_ask` at `9335-9377`. The question reads `"<stage> (<ctx>) attempt <n> failed: <reason>. Run it again?"` plus `rerun_carries` (9382-9390), which returns `""` for a workflow stage. The question says nothing about which copy will be reviewed.
21	- `scheduler.rs:9382-9390` `rerun_carries`: carry text only for `AttemptKind::Review` (code review), not plan review.
22	
23	### 3. The rerun decision and the note
24	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:3524-3530`: the `("rerun", "rerun")` arm reads `rerun_note(t, p, i)` then `retire_replaced(...)`.
25	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:8988-9013` `rerun_note`: returns `None` unless the stage kind is `Agent` or `Review` (8993-8997). A plan review is `StageKind::Workflow` (`dispatch/src/pipeline.rs:715-725`, `kind()`), so the `rerun` answer's own note is discarded for a plan review, and nothing is put into `t.rework`.
26	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:10599-10601` `sent_back`: "A workflow stage takes no note."
27	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:3578-3605` `retire_replaced`: marks the decision acted, saves, unmarks. It deletes no directory.
28	
29	### 4. The rerun itself
30	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:7379-7434` `workflow_stage`: for a latest attempt that is not open and not Complete, `may_rerun` (7402) → `start_workflow(... next_n ...)`.
31	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:7436-7530` `start_workflow`:
32	  - 7465-7470: `review_subject(t, &subject)` gives `(source_path, source_session)`.
33	  - 7471-7472: `std::fs::copy(&source_path, &copy)` where `copy = <attempt dir>/plan.md`, a new file under `review/<n>/joined/`. Note the new attempt is `n = next_n`, so attempt 2 gets `review/2/joined/plan.md`.
34	  - 7480-7487: `new_attempt(... AttemptState::Starting, BTreeMap::from([(subject, copy)]))`.
35	  - 7510-7520: `Body::WorkflowStart { source: source_session, plan: copy, ... }`.
36	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:10534-10548` `review_subject`: `t.attempts.iter().rev().filter(|a| a.state == AttemptState::Complete)` → first attempt with artifact `subject`; returns that attempt's path and `a.session`. Attempt 1 (Failed) is skipped; attempt `plan/1` (Complete) is picked. This is the reason for the bug. The rule ignores `forgotten` and lane visibility, so it is a third reader of the same question.
37	
38	### 5. The revise path (where the owner's note goes)
39	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:3495-3498`: `("finalize", "revise")` → `revise(...)` then `unmark`.
40	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:7565-7650` `revise`:
41	  - needs the run to be `Converged` or `AtCap` (7589-7603 region);
42	  - `round = view.round + 1`; `file = crate::report::round_file(&subject, round)` at 7616: `<stem>.feedback-<n>.md` **beside the reviewed copy**, i.e. `review/1/joined/plan.feedback-<round>.md`;
43	  - writes `"<OWNER_ROUND_HEADING>\n\n<note>"` with `atomic_write` (7617-7618);
44	  - `review.revisions.push(Revision { round, by, at_ms })` at 7621 on the attempt (`review/1`);
45	  - sends `Body::WorkflowObject { run, round, text }` (REVISE) to the app. On refusal it removes the file (7642).
46	- `dispatch/src/ticket.rs:510-516` `Revision { round, by, at_ms }`; `dispatch/src/ticket.rs:350` `Attempt.revisions`.
47	- `dispatch/src/report.rs:151-158` `round_file` / `beside`; `report.rs:165` `plan_round_numbers` lists the files that exist.
48	- `dispatch/src/lib.rs:102` `revisable` (finalize/revise pair); `lib.rs:95` mentions `revisions`.
49	
50	### 6. The revised copy
51	- The copy is `review/1/joined/plan.md`, the attempt's `artifacts["plan"]` (set in `start_workflow`'s `new_attempt` for attempt 1). Per `docs/design.md:2213-2216`, the review edits its copy in place under that one path. Nothing in the tree copies it out at revise time, and nothing reads it after the attempt fails.
52	- The app keeps round snapshots at `<data dir>/workflows/<run>/round-<n>/` (`src/core/workflow.rs:41`), per `docs/design.md:1000-1030`. Dispatch does not read them.
53	
54	### 7. The readers that disagree (the core of the bug)
55	| Reader | Rule | Location |
56	|---|---|---|
57	| Agent inputs (`input`, `input_where`, `lane_input`, `lane_plan`) | newest **Complete**, not forgotten | `ticket.rs:1437-1462`; `scheduler.rs:10843-10856` |
58	| Display (`shown`, `shown_where`, `shown_lane_files`) | newest Complete, or an **open** Workflow attempt | `ticket.rs:1467-1490`; `scheduler.rs:10900-10960` |
59	| Plan-review rerun source (`review_subject`) | newest **Complete** with artifact, plus its session | `scheduler.rs:10534-10548` |
60	
61	The existing unit test `ticket.rs:1827-1875` (`the_plan_shown_is_an_open_review_copy_but_an_input_never_is`) asserts that a Cancelled or Failed review copy is **not** shown as the plan (1856-1864: "A parked review's copy is not the plan going forward"). So "failed" and "parked" are treated the same by the current design. A fix that makes the failed copy the rerun's input must change that rule or add a distinction; the test is the constraint the planner has to face. The first test, `ticket.rs:1797`, asserts that a Failed plan attempt's input is skipped.
62	
63	Note on the session: `poll_workflow` writes the card's face into `Attempt.session` (`scheduler.rs:7784-7788`: `view.planner` or `view.reviewer`). So `review/1.session` is the review run's face, not the planning session. `review_subject` returns `a.session` alongside the path, so a fix that picks `review/1`'s copy by the same function would hand `WorkflowStart { source }` the wrong session unless it takes the planning session from `plan/1` (or from `review/1.run_sessions`, which `note_run_sessions` fills at `scheduler.rs:7710`). Design says the source is the *original* planning session (`docs/design.md:1000-1010`).
64	
65	### 8. What `show` prints (the "files:" block)
66	- `dispatch/src/main.rs:911-997` `show`. The `files:` block is at 980-995:
67	  - 982 `print_lane_files("plan", &p.plan_files)`: `plan: <path>` and, if `reviewing`, `(reviewed copy[, round N], review open)` (main.rs:896-908).
68	  - 984-989: `round`, `review summary`.
69	  - 991-994: `plan round N (owner): <feedback path>` from `p.plan_rounds`.
70	- `dispatch/src/serve.rs:538-600` `ticket_paths`:
71	  - 539-546 `plan_files = shown_lane_files(t, p, "plan")`; `reviewing` is `Workflow && is_open()`; `round = review_round(a)`.
72	  - 564-568 `review` = the **latest** Workflow attempt with artifacts. That is attempt 2 in the issue's repro, which has no round files yet. So `plan_rounds` (572) comes from attempt 2's copy and lists nothing, and the owner's round 2 that sits beside attempt 1's copy is not listed.
73	  - 570-571 `shown = t.shown("plan")`; `plan: shown.path`.
74	  - `serve.rs:504-523` `plan_rounds` and `serve.rs:526-534` `review_round` read round files and `Revision` entries of the given attempt only.
75	- The answered decision keeps the owner's note: `main.rs:1176-1198` `print_answered` prints `finalize [..]: answered revise by <who> — <note>` for every answered decision still on the ticket. So the note is visible under `answered:` while the decision is kept. The issue's "nothing warned" is true of the `files:` block and of the rerun question, not of the answered list.
76	
77	## On-disk record and rehydration (before the pane)
78	
79	Record and files, with the repro's paths:
80	- Ticket record under `<data>/tickets/<id>/` (`store.rs:147-149` `ticket_dir`). It holds `attempts` (`ticket.rs:266` `Attempt`), `decisions` (with the answered `revise` note), and `revisions` on `review/1`.
81	- Attempt directories: `ticket_dir/<stage>/<n>/<ctx>/` (`scheduler.rs:6303-6320` `attempt_dir`). Repro:
82	  - `plan/1/joined/plan.md`: the plan stage's output. Complete. Session: the plan stage's session on `plan/1`.
83	  - `review/1/joined/plan.md`: the copy of the plan at review start, edited in place by the review run, containing the revision. `review/1` is `Failed` with reason `review run gone: no such run`.
84	  - `review/1/joined/plan.feedback-2.md`: the owner's objection (`OWNER_ROUND_HEADING` + note). Keyed to round 2 of the app run. Also `plan.response-2.md` if the planner answered.
85	  - `review/1` `revisions`: `[{round: 2, by: "you", at_ms}]`.
86	  - `review/2/joined/plan.md`: fresh copy of `plan/1/joined/plan.md` made by `start_workflow` (7471).
87	- App side: the `WorkflowRun` in the project record of the Switchboard app's store (`src/core/model.rs:337`; persisted, `src/adapters/store.rs:1454`). It holds `plan` path, `rounds`, `state`, and round snapshots under `<data dir>/workflows/<run>/`.
88	
89	Rehydration after a Dispatch runner restart (the issue's trigger):
90	- The runner loads the ticket record and sees `review/1` as an open attempt with `run` set. `poll_workflow` asks the app. The app's answer is `no such run` (the issue's report). That fails the attempt, the record is saved as Failed, and a `rerun` question is asked (`rerun_ask`). Nothing reads `review/1/joined/plan.md` or the feedback file again.
91	- `rerun` answer: `rerun_note` → None; `retire_replaced` (saved); next pass `workflow_stage` → `may_rerun` true → `start_workflow(n=2)` → `review_subject` → `plan/1` → copy → `review/2/joined/plan.md` → `WorkflowStart` with the plan copy. The new app run starts from `plan/1`'s text; no objection is sent. `review/2` is then the only open workflow attempt, so `shown` names it.
92	
93	## What the pane shows now (from the code, not from running it)
94	
95	`show`, after the repro (attempt 2 running), prints in the `files:` block:
96	```
97	files:
98	  plan: <data>/tickets/<id>/review/2/joined/plan.md
99	    (reviewed copy, review open)
100	```
101	`round` is absent because `review_round(review/2)` is None (no round files, no revisions on review/2). There is no `plan round` line for round 2, and nothing names `review/1/joined/plan.md` or its feedback file as a plan. The `attempts` block shows `review/1 joined failed` and `review/2 joined running` (per the issue; `print_attempts` not read). The `answered:` list shows the revise note.
102	
103	The rerun question (for the failed review, before answering) is `review (joined) attempt 1 failed: review run gone: no such run. Run it again?` with options `rerun, park`. It does not say which copy will be reviewed.
104	
105	The Plan tab in the client reads `PathsView.plan` (= `review/2` copy), `plan_reviewed` and `plan_reviewing` (serve.rs:577-579). I did not read the Swift rendering in `client/`.
106	
107	## Tests in the tree that touch this
108	
109	- `dispatch/tests/first_slice.rs:3257-3287` `a_failed_review_run_fails_the_attempt_and_a_rerun_starts_a_new_run`: asserts a second run exists (`a.run.is_some()`) but does **not** assert which plan the rerun copied.
110	- `dispatch/tests/first_slice.rs:3817-3831` `a_run_switchboard_no_longer_has_fails_the_attempt` (`env.sb().runs.clear()`): asserts the `review run gone: no such run` reason and a `rerun` question.
111	- `dispatch/tests/first_slice.rs:3442-3500` `revise_writes_the_owners_round_and_sends_it_as_an_objection`: asserts the round file and `Revision`, not a rerun.
112	- No test combines `revise` with a failed review and a rerun. The gap is the test, not only the code.
113	- `dispatch/tests/support/mod.rs:690` fakes `no such run` for an absent run.
114	
115	## Other observations (tree facts)
116	
117	- `scheduler.rs:10081` `remove_dir_all(&ev.dir)` and `scheduler.rs:10154` `remove_file(path)`: evidence/secret removal. I did not check whether either can reach `review/<n>/` dirs.
118	- `review_subject` ignores `forgotten`, so a forgotten plan artifact on a Complete attempt is still copied. Pre-existing, unrelated to #187 except that a fix touching `review_subject` will meet it.
119	- The `rerun --note` on a plan review is dropped (see 3). The issue does not mention this, but it is the same loss.
120	
121	## What I did not check
122	
123	- I did not run `cargo test`, the dispatch tests, or any Dispatch/Switchboard command, and I did not reproduce the repro.
124	- I did not read the app's planner/reviewer prompts or `src/core/workflow.rs` in full (only `round_file`/snapshot line and `workflow` lookup). I did not confirm how the app edits the copy, or whether a killed run leaves it half-written.
125	- I did not read `print_attempts`, the `decide` CLI path, `events.rs` needs_note, or the Swift client.
126	- I did not read the rest of `design.md` (3,600 lines), only the sections above; the Milestone status sections are unread.
127	- I did not verify the issue's claims about attempt 2's content (round-1 points, the finalize result) or about the `09:28` timestamp.
128	- Claims about the Claude/Codex sessions are not in scope and were not checked.
129	
130	## Open questions
131	
132	- [tree] Does anything in `dispatch/src/` remove or overwrite `<ticket>/review/<n>/<ctx>/` (attempt dir) on retire, rerun, or restart? Settle by reading `retire_processes`, `remove_dir_all` at `scheduler.rs:10081`, and every `remove_file` on attempt paths.

The app drops a run only through `remove_workflow` (`src/core/workflow.rs:1009-1028`) or a store reset (Facts, Settled). This is a For-the-owner question (did the app lose the run?). The plan does not depend on the answer: the fix handles a failed review attempt of any reason. Which copy a rerun reads is derived, not stored: the rerun's source is the newest attempt of the same stage and context, if it is `Failed` and has the subject artifact and the file exists. `show` derives the same fact with the same rule, so the two cannot drift.

## The signals

None new. `shown` and `input` keep their rules, so the existing tests `dispatch/src/ticket.rs:1797` and `1827-1875` (a Failed or Cancelled review copy is not *the plan* going forward) stand. - `README.md`: no new file, no new environment variable; no Layout change.

One commit, README and design status updated, the app runs throughout.

Message: `Dispatch reruns a failed plan review from the failed attempt's copy and says so`

- `dispatch_control::LaneFile.revised_from: Option<PathBuf>` (additive, `#[serde(default)]`).
